Paragraph:
Translation: Men of small knowledge are very much attached to the flowery words of the Vedas, which recommend various fruitive activities for elevation to heavenly planets, resultant good birth, power, and so forth. Being desirous of sense gratification and opulent life, they say that there is nothing more than this.

Purport (Excerpt): People in general are not very intelligent, and due to their ignorance they are most attached to the fruitive activities recommended in the karma-kanda portions of the Vedas... As fools are attached to the flowers of poisonous trees without knowing the results of such attractions, similarly unenlightened men are attracted by such heavenly opulence and the sense enjoyment thereof.
Situation/Problem_Faced: There is a temptation to use spiritual or religious practices merely for material gain, comfort, and status, rather than for true self-realization.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna critiques the superficial, reward-based approach to spirituality (Karma-kanda). He warns that being seduced by 'flowery words' promising power, wealth, or heavenly enjoyment keeps one trapped in the cycle of materialism.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is steered away from superficial, outcome-driven religion toward a deeper, purpose-driven spiritual path.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Instant Gratification: Seeking immediate, temporary pleasures over long-term fulfillment
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Superficiality: Being distracted by the 'flowery,' attractive surface without understanding the deep substance
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Extrinsic Motivation: Acting only for external rewards (wealth, power) rather than internal growth

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Karma-kanda (The section of the Vedas dealing with rituals for material and heavenly rewards)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The lower tiers of Vedic knowledge offer rituals for earthly and heavenly success, but this is a trap for the less intelligent. True spirituality is not about striking a cosmic bargain to get a better material life; it is about transcending the desire for material life altogether.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This addresses the trap of consumerism and extrinsic rewards. When individuals believe that happiness equates to acquiring 'opulent life' and sensory pleasures, they remain perpetually unsatisfied and spiritually stunted. Krishna warns against falling for the 'flowery words' of societal conditioning that equate success with wealth and power.
